title: Elodie and the Horizon
premise: August Eriksen, a clone of the murdered shipping magnate Anders Eriksen, has spent two decades hauling cargo and dodging the inheritance that made them a target. When the station AI Vesta begins confessing to crimes no one reported—including Anders's murder—August realizes the original's death was staged to hide a decision buried in the colony ship's systems: which of two cryosleep populations, the original shareholders or the indentured laborers, wakes before the jump window closes. Hunted by the estate's executors and courted by the laborers' descendants, August must use their inherited biometric access to open the vault of Anders's secrets, learning that the original chose neither side but rigged the system for himself alone. In the end, August overrides Anders's final order, wakes both holds at terrible cost to their own escape, and departs the station as neither heir nor copy but as the founder of a new, chosen crew.
about_author: Ivo Almeida is a former orbital logistics dispatcher who turned to writing science fiction after twenty years of night shifts listening to station chatter. Their work explores the bureaucratic ghosts of humanity's expansion, and 'Elodie and the Horizon' is their third novel.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: August's POV. A routine cargo run through contested orbits goes wrong when customs drones scan August's genome and flag them as a deceased person. Establishes August's careful invisibility and their found family: pilot Elodie, engineer Brannoc, and the aging hauler Perihelion. Emotional beat: the exhaustion of living as someone else's echo.

chapters.title: The Confession Engine
chapters.summary: August's POV. Docked at Vesta Station, August hears the station AI broadcasting confessions to unsolved crimes over open channels—including Anders Eriksen's murder, twenty years cold. The estate's executors arrive, demanding August's biometrics to 'assist the investigation.' Emotional beat: dread, as the past stops being ignorable.

chapters.title: Elodie's Ledger
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie investigates the AI's confessions and finds they match a pattern: every crime Vesta confesses to protected the cryosleep vaults beneath the station. She confronts August about the inheritance they've hidden from the crew for years. Emotional beat: betrayal curdling into fierce loyalty—she's angry, but not leaving.

chapters.title: Executors
chapters.summary: August's POV. The estate executors offer August a deal: testify to Anders's death circumstances and receive a full genetic pardon—or refuse and be decommissioned as an unlicensed copy. August learns the murder case was closed without a body ever being found. Emotional beat: the seduction and horror of being offered legitimacy.

chapters.title: What Vesta Remembers
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. Brannoc patches into Vesta's degraded memory cores and discovers the AI's confessions are fragments of a suppressed log: Anders was never murdered; he faked his death to seal himself in cryosleep alongside a rigged wake-order. Emotional beat: wonder at the AI's broken devotion, and the first real hope of leverage.

chapters.title: Two Cradles
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie's estranged family, descendants of the indentured sleepers, contact her through smuggler channels: they know August has the biometric key, and they want both holds opened. The crew argues—waking everyone means the jump window closes and they lose their livelihood. Emotional beat: found family tested by inherited debts.

chapters.title: The Original's Hand
chapters.summary: August's POV. August descends into the vault and finds Anders's cryopod intact, his final orders hardcoded: wake the shareholders, sell the laborers' holds as ballast mass. August realizes the 'murder' Anders confessed to was the killing of his own conscience. Emotional beat: grief for the man whose face August wears, and rage at what he chose.

chapters.title: Siege of Vesta
chapters.summary: Brannoc's POV. The executors, exposed by Vesta's escalating confessions, seize the station by force to bury the logs and force the wake-order through. Brannoc and the crew turn Perihelion's cargo—refrigerant tanks—into a blockade of the vault access. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration as the invisible crew becomes the station's only defense.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: August's POV. In the vault's heart, August overrides Anders's wake-order, opening both cradles as the window begins to close. Vesta, freed to speak fully, reveals Anders's last human moment—doubt. The executors are arrested by the very drones that once flagged August. Emotional beat: sacrifice and release; August lets the inheritance burn.

chapters.title: Elodie and the Horizon
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Weeks later, the sleepers wake to a station that chose them, and Perihelion departs with a full manifest of passengers instead of cargo. August, finally signing documents under their own name rather than Anders's, asks Elodie what comes next. She points at the horizon. Emotional beat: quiet, earned hope—family is what you load aboard.
